scenario: TTL EXPIRY replayed ([LFST.9.1], [LFAC.1.3.3]). `Ping` lives 10_s; `seen` copies each Ping to `Seen`, and `gone` fires for a `Seen` whose Ping is no longer live. Ping a at 0, Ping b at 4_s, pumps at 11_s and 15_s: the pump-entry sweep expires a at the 11_s pump and b at the 15_s one, so `gone` fires once at each, and the expiry is visible only through WHEN `gone` fires. Nothing records an expiry as an input: the replay must re-derive it from its own sweep at the recorded clock. Paths: libds records through `rfcs/codec.c`'s recorder and replays through `ds_rfcs_replay_*` (pyds `Engine.record` / `Engine.replay`), which byte-compares each re-derived RuleFireAnnotation and FactEmit; the Mercury runtime records through `ds.rfcs` and replays through `ds.replay`.
rules_ds:
schema Ping scope ttl 10_s:
    k: String

schema Seen scope ttl 1_h:
    k: String

schema Gone scope ttl 1_h:
    k: String

rule seen:
    Ping p
->
    emit Seen k: p.k

rule gone:
    Seen s
    no Ping p where p.k == s.k
->
    emit Gone k: s.k
